sources.what: The correctness corpus's sources (G2 step 2): each repository and the revision read, what of it was read, and how. The oracle is SQLite 3.54.0 (Python's sqlite3 over the system library); translation is sqlglot 30.24.0. corpus.sh runs them: each `checkout` is a directory under CORPUS_SRC, at its `revision`.

oracle.through: Python 3.14 sqlite3, the system libsqlite3 (compile options in the run's record)

slt.name: sqllogictest
slt.upstream: https://www.sqlite.org/sqllogictest (fossil); the mirror carries its test tree unchanged
slt.read: test/**/*.test, all 622 files (evidence, index, random, select1-5), whole
slt.how: each file run on SQLite as slt_sqlite.c runs it (slt.py), its answers checked against the file's

duckdb.name: DuckDB's test suite
duckdb.read: test/sql/**/*.test and *.test_slow; a file is left out whole when it needs DuckDB's runner (require, load, restart, reconnect, loop, foreach, concurrentloop, mode, attach, unzip, test-env, tags)
duckdb.how: each record translated from DuckDB's dialect to SQLite's (sqlglot), run on SQLite, compared with DuckDB's expected answer; kept records written as sqllogictest files with SQLite's answers

cockroach.name: CockroachDB's logic tests
cockroach.how: as DuckDB's, read in PostgreSQL's dialect (CockroachDB's own); sessions a file switches between run on one connection

postgres.name: PostgreSQL's regression suite
postgres.read: src/test/regress/sql/*.sql except test_setup.sql, on the suite's base tables (test_setup.sql and data/*.data), written once as postgres/base.test, the fixture each file runs first
postgres.how: each statement translated and run on SQLite; run as written on PostgreSQL 17 (a container of the corpus's own) and the answers compared

kiln.name: kiln's own statements
kiln.revision_is: the commit production runs: KilnCD default/kiln-production's last deployment, image kiln:8adeadba572e164d4e2e342ba2a7d518c43d1b10 (2026-10-24 05:34Z)
kiln.read: every SQL string literal in crates/** at that revision (tests and vendor left out), and crates/kiln/src/store/migrations/*.sql, its production schema
kiln.how: kiln_queries.py: the schema made, then each statement run with its parameters unbound (NULL), written as one sqllogictest file with SQLite's answers

written.name: the written cases
written.how: at least ten cases for every inventory entry, and families for the step's named features (window frames, recursive CTEs, JSON, UPSERT and RETURNING, generated columns, STRICT, collations, triggers, PRAGMAs), each group its own file with SQLite's answers

duckdb.why: the same SQL means something else on SQLite (affinity, NULL and type rules, a function's own semantics)
a type SQLite doesn't have (wide and unsigned integers, DECIMAL, intervals, time zones, UUID, BIT, ENUM, nested types): SQLite reads the value by affinity
the same rows in another order (no ORDER BY, or ties under it)
a row count from data the translation couldn't carry: rows a COPY from a file, a statement SQLite refused, or another session made
dates and times: SQLite keeps them as text or numbers, with functions of its own
the engine's own catalog (PRAGMAs, information_schema, pg_catalog, duckdb_*, crdb_internal, SHOW)
